audit.why: Early is firmly Viktor's (Kassadin weak to magic pre-items), first item is Kassadin's equalizer, late depends on the converted lead. Content layer and packet chart agree; matches 50.25% WR over 3222 games.
Spikes: 3-5 punish window, 6 still Viktor's, first item is HIS equalizer, late conditional. Content spikes[] carries all four correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Viktor's E called 'Death Ray' in whys[2], spikes[0].text and content early. Null Sphere's magic shield and the Nether Blade auto-reset tell are never stated. breakdown.cooldowns has no digit and misses that Riftwalk is a 5s-base blink.
audit.why: Kit: E is Hextech Ray. His Q grants a shield that absorbs magic damage — your whole kit is magic, so forcing it changes the burst math. His W is an auto reset (the combo tell). Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s, 500 range.
Riftwalk 5s base is effectively always up post-6; his E needs 21-17s plus nearby spell charges; your W 17s.

edits.before: This is your window to punish. Kassadin is helpless against magic damage pre-6, so sweep E (Death Ray) through the wave and onto him every time he steps to CS, and use W (Gravity Field) to lock him if he tries to close the gap. Shove and deny him levels.
edits.after: This is your window to punish. Kassadin is helpless against magic damage pre-6, so sweep E (Hextech Ray) through the wave and onto him every time he steps to CS, and use W (Gravity Field) to lock him if he tries to close the gap. Shove and deny him levels.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Gravity Field has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 — post-6 it is effectively always up, so track his mana, not the cooldown. - Force Pulse needs 21s plus nearby spell charges; if he hasn't seen spells it isn't ready. - Your W is 17s: one job, the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: E through the wave into his chest, Q-shield the response, empowered-auto, and walk — a full trade where his answer hit a shield.
edits.after: His Null Sphere shield absorbs magic damage — poke it out with E from behind minions first, then the real trade lands on health bar.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: His combo opens with the Nether Blade auto-reset — at half HP that wind-up plus Riftwalk is a kill script; back off before it starts.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: Don’t cast E at melee-adjacent range once his all-in is loaded — your long cast time is the window he dives through.
